Title: Sargon Wastes a Minute of Our Time

Messages.Author: NoSoup4you
Messages.Body:
I've been playing VTES for a couple years now, and I was pleased last week because I finally managed to build a "creative" deck that felt competitive. It won a 4p, running out of cards in the process (!), and I've been iterating on it since then. I didn't expect to see another Inside Dirt deck  win a tournament at the same time, but figured if the card is being taken seriously now, I could try posting my own deck here.

This has a couple minor refinements from the version I played at our last meeting here, but the actions and modifiers remain the same. The thing I've waffled on the most is the blood and pool gain.

How do you intend to oust?

Inside Dirt two or three times per turn.

How do you intend to keep from being ousted?

Going forward fast, Barrenness and/or Inside Dirt backwards. Noncommital defense overall, just hoping to burn a vampire or two and block with Sargon once in awhile.

What do you want your ready region to look like?

Sargon and three !nos.

What do you want your average turn to look like?

Two or three Sargon actions, two or three Inside Dirts.

What's your metagame like? How do your opponents play?

Every deck type shows up, but not a lot of the top ones - no one plays Malk 94, MMPA, speed Legionnaires etc, either out of boredom or politeness. There are some weird pet decks that get played a lot, like Horsehoes+Touch of Pain or Zizi Bauble.

What problems have you observed with the deck in play?

It ran out of cards quickly, so I'm trying Sargon Fragment as a bit of recursion. Blood could get low with all the Forgotten Labyrinth, but inferior obf necessitates running them I think. Rush combat is a bit worrying. The group 2 crypt is really bad for obfuscate weenies.

This might be better, but I haven't played it yet. You free up master slots and get something to do in combat, in exchange for a slow start.

I'm mainly wondering whether to pursue it with the oversized weenies or the midcaps. Also thinking about including 2-4 Evil Eye, though it's easy to start going down a bad path with all the things that "could" be in here.

I'm guessing the Night Moves version is going to be better than this deck, but I find Sargon's bullshit actions funny.

Messages.Author: kschaefer
Messages.Body: You have a lot of Masters, Some of which you may not care about at various points in the game. You also have Sargon as a star. Consider Path of the Void for him. He's never going to bleed, won't be affected by the Path's drawback and might even be able to shed extra Masters in the unlock phase. The perma-stealth would be useful and occasionally hitting an empty vampire for 1 damage could be good.

Messages.Author: NoSoup4you
Messages.Body:
Newest version

I often got 1 or 2 VPs with the original attempt, but I've been gradually transitioning towards playing a little defense. I cut some of the "dead end" actions for Sargon, hopefully leaving him unlocked most turns except for oust attempts. For example, it probably wasn't worth effectively paying 3 pool for Hell's Fury, or 2 pool to get and start using Kaymakli. Veneficti is still awesome. Clan Impersonation could go, but the option of playing Dirt and getting the edge in the same action later is powerful.

Main line of (still casual) defense will be Evil Eye with occasional blocking, and Archon as a speedbump. The downside is that there's no good answer to bumped bleeds for 3. Barrenness backwards is still solid, though hard to choose the right vampire sometimes. Maybe better to hit full vampires instead of trying too hard to build up for the superior.

I threw in a couple wakes too as they're easily cycled, but I'm still worried about diluting the unlock+dirt+stealth combos. Morpheus would be logical, but Qui Vive lets you Evil Eye and cycles better.

The hard part of playing the deck is still having the wisdom to "waste" an Inside Dirt on something besides 3 pool. I've dug myself into a malk 94 playstyle with the deck, and need to convince everyone that it can do other things now. I actually have a lot of freedom in who I target with things, but people here aren't big on deals.

Still wondering: smaller crypt with inferior obf, or midcap version? I'm not getting blocked that often. Also considering a second Shannon here instead of Ox, as 5+3 makes for a good opening crypt.

Messages.Author: NoSoup4you
Messages.Body: After a few plays, the more "well rounded" midcap one hasn't performed that well. Evil Eye as your main defense means you're tempted to let cardless bleeds through, and the game is almost unwinnable if you aren't able to get out three vampires. I will probably go back to the smaller crypt relying more on Forgotten Labyrinth. On the other hand, I've made some refinements since then that will still be helpful.
